name: Pec Deck Peak Contraction
description: A pec deck flye variation where each repetition includes a deliberate 2–3 second isometric hold at the fully contracted position (arms together in front). This peak contraction technique maximizes tension on the pectoralis major at its shortest length, where the muscle generates a powerful squeeze. The paused technique is used specifically to develop the mind-muscle connection and improve the ability to feel and contract the chest at peak.

execution.starting_position: Sit in a pec deck machine with the back fully against the pad. Grip the handles or place forearms in the arm pads. Begin with arms open to the sides at shoulder height.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust the seat height so the arms are at shoulder level when in the starting position. Adjust the starting-width to allow a full range of motion without shoulder discomfort. Select a moderate, controllable weight.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms open, feeling the chest stretch.
Step 2: Drive the arms together in a sweeping arc.
Step 3: At full contraction — arms as close together as the machine allows — hold the position for 2–3 seconds. Squeeze the chest as hard as possible.
Step 4: Return under control to the starting position, feeling the full stretch. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as arms come together, hold breath briefly during the peak isometric, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Releasing the squeeze immediately at the top instead of holding the contraction
Using momentum to swing the arms together — slow and deliberate movement is essential
Shoulder blades lifting off the back pad during the squeeze
safety_considerations: Keep the back fully in contact with the seat back throughout
Adjust the starting width if shoulder discomfort occurs at the open position
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full range from maximum comfortable stretch to full contraction. The key is the held peak at the top.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2-3-2-1 (2s sweep in, 3s peak hold, 2s return, 1s stretch)
coaching_cues: Squeeze as hard as you possibly can at the top — try to touch your elbows together
The hold is not a rest — it is the most important part of each rep
